faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: 'In an ideal coil the back-emf balances the supply at every instant' is asserted with no reason, and it is the step the whole lag rests on.
faults.fix: Add the reason: with no resistance there is nothing else in the coil for the supply's voltage to appear across, so the back-emf must match it at every instant.

faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: The 2π argument says the arm's tip travels 2π radii a turn but not why that is the wave's slope at the crossing; and 'the current settles at half the size' skips that the supply fixes the current's steepest slope.
faults.fix: Say the tip is moving straight up as the wave crosses zero, so the wave rises at the tip's speed; and that the back-emf must equal the supply, so the steepest slope is fixed, and at twice the frequency that slope is reached with half the peak.

faults.fault: false absolute / a claim that fails after a later idea
faults.where: explain, opening and bold takeaway; practice rule of thumb
faults.finding: 'A coil's voltage follows how fast its current is changing, not how big it is' and 'the current lags by a quarter cycle' read alone are false for a real coil with resistance (lesson 6 has R and L together, where the lag is less).
faults.fix: Make it the back-emf that follows the rate of change, and the quarter-cycle lag 'in an ideal coil' / 'close to a quarter cycle when its resistance is small'.

faults.fault: numbers that do not check from the shown figures
practice not standing on its own
faults.finding: 'the example coil' means nothing in the dossier, and '318 V across the opening gap' overstates what the rule gives, which is the coil's back-emf.
faults.fix: Name the 31.8 mH coil and call the 318 V the coil's back-emf while the current falls.

faults.fault: an analogy that maps the wrong quantity
faults.finding: 'it travels less each way' maps current to distance; the lesson maps current to speed.
faults.fix: 'it never gets up to as much speed each way'.

faults.fault: re-teaching an earlier course without saying so
faults.finding: Complex numbers lesson 7 already gave X_L = 2πfL; the lesson should say it is the formula he has met, now with its cause, not present it as new.
faults.fix: 'You met X_L = 2πfL in Complex numbers lesson 7; here is where it comes from.'

shape.rule in words: yes: the back-emf is L times the rate of change of current; X_L = supply voltage ÷ current = 2πfL
shape.worked example with real numbers: yes: 31.8 mH, 100 V peak, 10 A at 50 Hz, 8.33 A at 60 Hz, 5 A at 100 Hz; the 100 mH mains coil in practice
shape.misconception shown failing: yes: biggest current, biggest voltage (screen 2); current leads, and half a cycle (screen 4, the Indonesian study's misread graph); current scaled up with frequency (screens 6, 11, 12); volts × amps as watts (screens 8, 12); the ohmmeter reading as AC opposition (screen 10)
shape.analogy from his trade with where it bre: yes: the cable drum turned to and fro; breaks on fixed mass against core-dependent inductance, and on mutual induction
shape.put it into practice: yes: safety first, steps, rule of thumb, worked example, mistakes
